title: Allocation of contractual risk
summary: Risk allocation determines which party must bear the consequences when a relevant assumption proves wrong or an event makes performance more difficult or less valuable.
notes:
Allocation may be expressed through conditions, warranties, fixed prices, or force-majeure clauses. It may also follow from the undertaking interpreted in context and the governing legal rules. Stees, Taylor, Transatlantic, and Krell illustrate different relationships among the promised result, the disrupted circumstances, and the claimed excuse.

Foreseeability is relevant, but asking whether an event could have been imagined does not finish the inquiry. A party may know a risk exists without clearly assuming every consequence; conversely, an unconditional undertaking may place a risk on that party. Explain the language, commercial purpose, alternatives, and burden rather than using “risk” as an unexplained label.
